To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Female sticklebacks prefer male MHC ligands that match the immunogenetic status of their own population, and this preference is based on the assessment of the number of MCH alleles of their potential mates.

1) female sticklebacks use olfactory cues of male MHC peptide ligand mixtures during mate choice; 2) females of the river and lake ecotype prefer male odours with an optimal immunogenetic signature of their own habitat; 3) the olfactory cue that females use to assess male immunogenetic status is a mixture of synthetic MHC peptides that mimics the optimal number of MHC peptide liganders of their own ecotype.
female stickleback fish use male odour to choose mates with optimal immunogenetic complementarities.

the role of the major histocompbility complex (MHC) in the process of speciation.

the female sticklebacks are able to assess the immunogenetic status of the male and choose the optimal male based on the immunogenetic diversity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

females of three-spined stickleback populations that differ in their immunogenetic composition and in the local parasite fauna prefer males that have a number of MHC peptide ligand variants that optimizes the immunogenetic diversity of their offspring.

female three-spined stickleback (Gasterosteidae, Gasterosteus aculetus) can use the olfactory system to assess the immunogenetic status of their prospective mates and that they prefer males with an optimal number of MHC peptide ligand variants that are characteristic for their local environment.
females of a stickleback ecotype that is adapted to a particular habitat prefer males of the same ecotype, and that they use MHC-associated odours to identify ecotypically appropriate males.
The main takeaway from our work is that
females of many vertebrate taxa use male odours to assess immunogenetic complementation of their prospective mates.
female mate choice can be used as a tool for functional validation of the molecular basis of ecological speciation.
